source.title: Efficient compression in color naming and its evolution
source.venue: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America

confidence_rationale: Colour-naming systems across languages sit near the optimal information-bottleneck frontier trading lexicon complexity against accuracy, where accuracy is the listener's ability to reconstruct the speaker's intended meaning. That is ARC-117's receiver-uncertainty objective operating at the level of the lexicon, across real languages, with a single trade-off parameter. Discounted because it concerns what a language makes available, not moment-to-moment message selection by an individual sender, and because the IB accuracy term is a reconstruction objective rather than a coordination-cost objective.
failure_signatures: The fit is to cross-linguistic lexicons (population-level, evolutionary timescale), not to individual utterance choice, so it cannot adjudicate ARC-117's per-message prediction.

IB systems leave large regions of colour space inconsistently named -- efficient communication tolerates substantial residual receiver uncertainty when the complexity cost is high, so 'minimises' should be read as 'trades off', not as absolute minimisation.

mapping.source_claim_statement: Languages efficiently compress meanings into words by optimising the information-bottleneck trade-off between lexicon complexity and accuracy; colour-naming systems across languages are near-optimal on this trade-off, and variation in one trade-off parameter accounts for much of the cross-language variation.
mapping.ree_translation: In IB terms the speaker encodes a meaning and the listener reconstructs it; 'accuracy' is how well the listener's reconstructed belief matches the speaker's. ARC-117's claim that utterances approximate a receiver-sufficient statistic is the per-message version of this lexicon-level objective. Its near-optimality across languages is evidence that receiver reconstruction, not sender salience alone, shapes what a communication system can say.
mapping.mapping_caveat: Population-level, evolved lexicon rather than an individual agent's online message policy; the 'receiver' is an idealised listener sharing a need distribution. Evidence that the objective shapes the code, not that each sender computes it. The complexity term makes the objective a trade-off, so ARC-117's 'minimises' overstates it.
mapping.source_context: World Color Survey naming data from 110+ languages analysed against the information-bottleneck frontier; simulated evolution of IB-optimal systems.

confidence_components.notes: PNAS, large cross-linguistic dataset, extended since to other semantic domains. Mapping discounted for level (lexicon vs message) rather than for direction.
